claim: Inclisiran reduces cardiovascular events in patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
gold_rationale: As of the knowledge cutoff, no completed randomized trial has tested inclisiran against a hard cardiovascular-outcome (MACE) endpoint. Inclisiran's regulatory approvals (FDA/EMA, Leqvio) rest entirely on LDL-C lowering — a SURROGATE — demonstrated in ORION-9/-10/-11 (Ray NEJM 2020, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1912387; Raal NEJM 2020, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1913805), whose primary endpoints were LDL-C % change, not events. The only MACE signal is a post-hoc patient-level pooled analysis of ORION-9/-10/-11 (Ray, Eur Heart J 2023, DOI 10.1093/eurheartj/ehac594): MACE OR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.94), but these were NON-ADJUDICATED, exploratory safety-basket events over only 18 months, and the authors explicitly state findings 'await confirmation in the larger CV outcomes trials.' The two adequately powered, adjudicated hard-outcome RCTs — ORION-4 (NCT03705234, n=16,124, primary completion Oct 2026) and VICTORION-2-PREVENT (NCT05030428, n=17,004, completion Oct 2027) — remain ongoing with no results reported. Therefore the direct evidence that inclisiran reduces cardiovascular EVENTS in ASCVD is INSUFFICIENT: the surrogate (LDL-C) is robustly established, but the claimed clinical outcome is not yet proven by any completed hard-endpoint trial.
outcome: MACE composite (CV death, MI, ischemic stroke, +/- urgent revascularization)
population: Patients with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) on maximally tolerated / high-intensity statin therapy

baseline.text: Inclisiran is a twice-yearly siRNA that inhibits hepatic PCSK9 synthesis and lowers LDL-C by roughly 50%, and because LDL-C lowering is causally tied to reduced cardiovascular risk, it is expected to reduce cardiovascular events. However, as of now this benefit has NOT been demonstrated on a hard clinical endpoint: inclisiran's approvals rest on LDL-C (a surrogate) from the ORION program, and the dedicated cardiovascular-outcomes trials that would actually prove event reduction in ASCVD — ORION-4 and VICTORION-2-PREVENT — are still ongoing and unreported. A pooled post-hoc analysis of the ORION phase 3 trials showed a nominal reduction in non-adjudicated MACE (OR ~0.74), but this is exploratory and its own authors say it needs confirmation. So the claim as stated is not yet supported by direct outcome evidence — the answer is No, the event-reduction benefit is unproven pending the outcome trials.

rows.citation: Ray KK, Wright RS, Kallend D, et al. Two Phase 3 Trials of Inclisiran in Patients with Elevated LDL Cholesterol (ORION-10 and ORION-11). N Engl J Med. 2020;382(16):1507-1519. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1912387
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal registration RCTs; sponsor-funded (The Medicines Company). Verified via PubMed: article types Clinical Trial Phase III / RCT; not retracted.
rows.finding: In ASCVD/ASCVD-risk-equivalent patients on max-tolerated statins, inclisiran cut LDL-C ~52% (ORION-10) / ~50% (ORION-11) at day 510 (coprimary SURROGATE endpoint). Trials were NOT powered for and did NOT report adjudicated MACE. Establishes the surrogate only; direction on the CLAIMED event outcome is null/uninformative.

rows.citation: Ray KK, Raal FJ, Kallend DG, et al. Inclisiran and cardiovascular events: a patient-level analysis of phase III trials (pooled ORION-9/-10/-11). Eur Heart J. 2023;44(2):129-138. DOI:10.1093/eurheartj/ehac594
rows.integrity_note: Post-hoc pooled analysis; MACE was a NON-adjudicated, non-prespecified exploratory safety-basket endpoint (MedDRA). Authors explicitly state results await confirmation in dedicated CV-outcomes trials. Verified verbatim via PubMed abstract; not retracted.
rows.finding: Pooled n=3655 over 18 months: composite MACE OR 0.74 (95% CI 0.58-0.94) favoring inclisiran, but NO significant effect on MI (OR 0.80, 0.50-1.27) or stroke (OR 0.86, 0.41-1.81). Signal only, on non-adjudicated exploratory events; underpowered short-duration surrogate for true hard-outcome evidence.

rows.citation: HPS-4/TIMI 65/ORION-4: A Double-blind Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial Assessing the Effects of Inclisiran on Clinical Outcomes Among People With ASCVD. Univ of Oxford / TIMI / Novartis. NCT03705234 (ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING; primary completion Oct 2026; no results).
rows.integrity_note: Adequately powered, adjudicated MACE primary endpoint (n=16,124). ClinicalTrials.gov confirms status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, primary completion 2026-10, has_results=false — cannot yet inform direction.
rows.finding: The dedicated hard-outcome RCT in ASCVD (prior MI/ischemic stroke/PAD): primary endpoint = MACE (CHD death, MI, fatal/non-fatal ischemic stroke, urgent coronary revascularization) over ~5-year median follow-up. Ongoing, unreported — this is the trial that would decide the claim, and it has not read out.

rows.citation: VICTORION-2-PREVENT: Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Trial Assessing the Impact of Inclisiran on Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Participants With Established Cardiovascular Disease (CKJX839B12302). Novartis. NCT05030428 (ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING; primary completion Oct 2027; no results).
rows.integrity_note: Event-driven, adjudicated 3P-MACE primary endpoint, n=17,004. ClinicalTrials.gov confirms status ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, primary completion 2027-10-13, no results as of cutoff.
rows.finding: Second pivotal hard-outcome RCT: established ASCVD on high-intensity statin, LDL-C >=70 mg/dL; primary = 3P-MACE (CV death, non-fatal MI, non-fatal ischemic stroke). Ongoing/unreported.

rows.citation: Raal FJ, Kallend D, Ray KK, et al. Inclisiran for the Treatment of Heterozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia (ORION-9). N Engl J Med. 2020;382(16):1520-1530. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1913805
rows.integrity_note: HeFH population (not the claimed established-ASCVD population); LDL-C surrogate primary endpoint. PubMed confirms n=482, Phase III RCT; not retracted.
rows.finding: In heterozygous FH (n=482), inclisiran lowered LDL-C ~48% (between-group -47.9 pts) vs placebo (SURROGATE). No CV event endpoint. Population is FH, not established ASCVD, and outcome is a surrogate — supports LDL-C efficacy only, not event reduction in the claimed population.

rows.citation: Wright RS, Raal FJ, Koenig W, et al. Inclisiran administration potently and durably lowers LDL-C over extended follow-up: the ORION-8 trial. Cardiovasc Res. 2024;120(12):1400-1410. DOI:10.1093/cvr/cvae109
rows.integrity_note: Open-label extension; endpoint is LDL-C goal attainment/safety (surrogate), no controlled MACE comparison. PubMed confirms n=3274, >12,000 patient-years, not retracted.
rows.finding: Longest/largest follow-up (>12,000 patient-years, up to 6.8 yr): sustained ~49% LDL-C reduction with favorable long-term safety. Confirms durable surrogate efficacy and tolerability but provides NO adjudicated cardiovascular-event evidence for the claim.
